note:
Hand-triaged for the 1.8.0 release gate (Free+Pro paired run). Each suppression was individually verified; nothing was bulk-baselined. False positives are scanner limits (dynamic hook/key resolution); graceful-gap items read with sane defaults and are tracked as 'add admin field' enhancements, not runtime breaks. 2.2.0 gate additions (2026-07-23): three AS/WP-Cron constant-fired hooks individually verified as false positives.

2026-09-03 (2.4.1 retag): 12 further errors triaged individually, none bulk-baselined. ELEVEN were verified false positives and are suppressed below with the mechanism that hides them from the audit — in every case the write or the fire happens through a class constant, a dynamically-built key, or a scheduler (wp_schedule_event / as_enqueue_async_action) rather than a string literal in a do_action/update_option call. The TWELFTH was a REAL BUG and was fixed, not suppressed: 'user_meta-read-never-written:_mvs_extra_document_credits' was correct — QuotaService::add_credits() guarded on MEDIA_TYPES (the MIME-detectable list, which deliberately excludes documents) instead of SUMMARY_TYPES (the metered list, which includes them), so document credits could never be granted while deduct_credit() had no such guard and would spend them. See the comment at that guard.

False positive, verified 2026-09-03 AT RUNTIME. Written by Quota\QuotaService::increment_usage(), which builds the key dynamically as '_mvs_' . $media_type . '_count' and explicitly maps a document by its media_type rather than its MIME. Proven by calling increment_usage() on a real document: the meta went from '' to '1'. DocumentIngestService fires mvs_media_uploaded, which is what invokes it.

Suppressed ONLY because the bug it reported has been FIXED — this entry is not a 'verified exception', it is a scar. The audit was RIGHT: Quota\QuotaService::add_credits() guarded on MEDIA_TYPES (the MIME-detectable list, which excludes documents by design) instead of SUMMARY_TYPES (the metered list, which includes them), so add_credits( $user, 'document', N ) returned false and wrote nothing. Document credits could never be granted, while deduct_credit() has no such guard and increment_usage() calls it for documents over the package limit. Fixed 2026-09-03; proven at runtime — add_credits() now takes the key from '' to '3'. The finding persists only because the write builds the key dynamically as '_mvs_extra_' . $media_type . '_credits', which a literal scan cannot see. If this ever fires again after a refactor, re-verify at RUNTIME before assuming it is noise.
